STORY × TECHNOLOGY × CREATIVITY × COMMUNITY
THE OPPORTUNITY
Creating a dedicated home for creative minds on campus. The campus currently has no dedicated film club or structured film-focused
platform for students interested in filmmaking, cinematography, editing, sound, acting, visual storytelling and creative production.
INNOV8 Film Technology is proposed to fill this gap by bringing creative and technical students together in one sustained ecosystem.
VISION
To establish INNOV8 Film Technology as a student-driven creative and technical ecosystem where students learn, experiment,
collaborate and produce.

AI & PROMPT ENGINEERING DOMAIN
Vision • Innovation • Research • Events • Excellence
VISION
To establish a student-driven AI innovation and research ecosystem that transforms students
from AI users into AI creators, researchers and innovators through practical learning,
experimentation, project development and external exposure.
KEY OBJECTIVES
01 | SKILL DEVELOPMENT
Build practical expertise in Generative AI, Prompt Engineering, LLMs, AI Agents,
Automation, Multimodal AI and AI-assisted Development through hands-on learning.
02 | EVENTS & CHALLENGES
Conduct engaging activities such as Prompt Battles, AI Creation Challenges, Ideathons, AI
Build Challenges, AI Hackathons and Innovation Showcases.

Create a continuous pipeline from Problem → Idea → Prototype → Testing → Solution,

Establish an AI Research Cell where students explore research problems, study existing work,

Collaborate with Gaming, Film Technology, Dance and other technical domains to develop

06 | COMPETITIONS & EXTERNAL EXPOSURE
Prepare and mentor teams for Hackathons, AI Competitions, Innovation Challenges, Project

SIGNATURE INITIATIVES
AI Research Cell — Student-led research, paper discussions, experiments and publications.
AI Innovation Lab — A platform for rapid experimentation, prototyping and exploration of
emerging AI technologies.

AI Challenge Series — Recurring competitions focused on Prompt Engineering, AI Creation,
Automation and AI Problem Solving.
AI Innovation Showcase — Annual demonstration of student projects, research and prototypes.
AI Knowledge Repository — A continuously growing collection of research papers,
experiments, resources and project documentation for future members.

Dance Domain – Expected Outcomes
By the end of the current semester, the Dance Domain of INNOV8 aims to achieve the
following outcomes:
1. Basic Dance Skill Development
Students will learn and practice fundamental dance movements, steps, rhythm,
coordination, and basic choreography.
2. Choreography Development
The team will create and complete at least 2–3 original group choreographies suitable
for college events and competitions.
3. Performance Readiness
Students will be trained to perform confidently as a coordinated team on stage.
4. Regular Practice System
A structured practice schedule will be established, with designated student
coordinators responsible for managing rehearsals.

5. Team Formation
A dedicated INNOV8 Dance Team will be formed with interested students and
assigned responsibilities such as choreography, performance, coordination, and
practice management.
6. College Event Participation
The team will be prepared to participate in suitable department-level, college-level,
and inter-college cultural events and competitions, subject to approval and
opportunities.

7. Student Skill Portfolio
Students will document their performances, choreographies, and participation to build

8. Leadership and Teamwork
Students will gain practical experience in coordination, group management, rehearsal

9. AI-Integrated Creative Exploration
Where appropriate, the team will explore AI-assisted tools for music selection,
choreography ideation, movement analysis, visual concepts, and performance
planning, while keeping the actual dance training and performance student-driven.

Unit 1: Advanced Relational Database Normalization.
Boyce-Codd Normal Form BCNF is a stricter definition of normalization than 3NF.
A relation schema R is in BCNF with respect to a set F of functional dependencies if,
for all functional dependencies X -> Y in F+, at least one of the following holds:
1. X -> Y is a trivial functional dependency Y is a subset of X.
2. X is strictly a superkey for relation schema R.
Unlike Third Normal Form 3NF, BCNF does not permit the exception where Y is a prime attribute.

BCNF Decomposition and Lossless Joins.
Any relation schema can be decomposed into a collection of BCNF schemas with a lossless join.
However, BCNF decomposition is not always dependency-preserving.
When decomposing a relation into BCNF, we identify a dependency X -> Y that violates BCNF,
and decompose R into R - Y and X union Y.
We repeat this process until all decomposed relations satisfy Boyce-Codd Normal Form.
